req.title: Delete post
req.statement: The system shall remove the post row and redirect to / when POST /<id>/delete is issued by the post's author.

doc.reasoning: The requirement states that POST /<id>/delete issued by the post's author must delete the post row and redirect to /. We need: (1) a positive test confirming the author can delete their own post and is redirected to /, and the row is gone from the DB; (2) a negative test confirming a non-author (different user) gets 403; (3) a boundary test confirming that deleting a non-existent post ID returns 404; (4) an additional negative test for unauthenticated access (redirected to login); (5) a state-transition test confirming the post is truly absent after deletion. All tests use the pre-loaded fixture data (user id=1 'test'/'test', user id=2 'other'/'other', post id=1 authored by user 1).

tests.name: test_delete_post_by_author_redirects_to_index
preconditions: App initialized with test database containing pre-loaded fixture data
Post id=1 exists and is authored by user id=1
expected: Post id=1 no longer exists in the database
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import get_db

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
with app.app_context():
    from flaskr.db import init_db
    init_db()

client = app.test_client()

def test_delete_post_by_author_redirects_to_index():
    with client.session_transaction() as sess:
        sess.clear()
    r_login = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'test', 'password': 'test'})
    assert r_login.status_code == 302
    r_delete = client.post('/1/delete')
    assert r_delete.status_code == 302
    assert r_delete.headers['Location'] == '/'
    with app.app_context():
        db = get_db()
        post = db.execute('SELECT id FROM post WHERE id = 1').fetchone()
        assert post is None

test_delete_post_by_author_redirects_to_index()

tests.name: test_delete_post_state_transition_row_absent_after_delete
preconditions: App initialized with test database containing pre-loaded fixture data
actions: Verify post id=1 exists before deletion
Verify post id=1 does not exist after deletion
Verify index page at / does not contain 'test title'
expected: Before delete: post row with id=1 is present
After delete: post row with id=1 is absent
After delete: GET / returns 200 and does not contain 'test title'
trace: R-FLASKR-021: row deleted state transition; redirect to / confirmed
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import get_db

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
with app.app_context():
    from flaskr.db import init_db
    init_db()

client = app.test_client()

def test_delete_post_state_transition_row_absent_after_delete():
    with client.session_transaction() as sess:
        sess.clear()
    with app.app_context():
        db = get_db()
        pre = db.execute('SELECT id FROM post WHERE id = 1').fetchone()
        assert pre is not None
        assert pre['id'] == 1
    r_login = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'test', 'password': 'test'})
    assert r_login.status_code == 302
    r_delete = client.post('/1/delete')
    assert r_delete.status_code == 302
    assert r_delete.headers['Location'] == '/'
    with app.app_context():
        db = get_db()
        post = db.execute('SELECT id FROM post WHERE id = 1').fetchone()
        assert post is None
    r_index = client.get('/')
    assert r_index.status_code == 200
    assert b'test title' not in r_index.data

test_delete_post_state_transition_row_absent_after_delete()
